description: CropGuard pest / disease / deficiency class registry for the Smart Farming Assistant edge model. 'aliases' hold upstream dataset folder names (PlantVillage, IP102, Rice Leaf Diseases, ...) so public datasets can be remapped onto this taxonomy without renaming files.

classes.name: Background / non-leaf
classes.symptoms: Soil, sky, hand, machinery or an out-of-focus frame with no diagnosable leaf surface.

classes.name: Healthy tomato
classes.symptoms: Uniform green lamina, turgid leaflets, no lesions or chlorosis.

classes.name: Healthy potato
classes.symptoms: Dark green compound leaves, no necrotic spots.

classes.name: Healthy rice
classes.symptoms: Erect green blades, no lesions, no hopper burn.

classes.name: Healthy wheat
classes.symptoms: Uniform green flag and lower leaves, no pustules.

classes.name: Healthy maize
classes.symptoms: Broad green leaves, intact whorl, no windowpane feeding.

classes.name: Healthy cotton
classes.symptoms: Dark green palmate leaves, no vein thickening or curling.

classes.name: Healthy chilli
classes.symptoms: Flat glossy leaves, no upward curling or silvering.

classes.name: Healthy sugarcane
classes.symptoms: Green blades, no red streaks in split cane, no dead hearts.

classes.name: Healthy grape
classes.symptoms: Uniform green lamina, no oil spots or pustules.

classes.name: Early blight
classes.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern) and a yellow halo, starting on the oldest lower leaves.

classes.name: Late blight
classes.symptoms: Water-soaked grey-green blotches turning brown-black, spreading fast from leaf tip/margin, white downy growth on the underside in humid weather.

classes.name: Septoria leaf spot
classes.symptoms: Many small circular spots with grey centres and dark margins, black pycnidia visible in the centre.

classes.name: Bacterial spot
classes.symptoms: Small greasy water-soaked spots that become angular, dark and scabby; leaf edges tatter.

classes.name: Leaf mould
classes.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on the upper surface with olive-green velvety mould directly beneath; typical of polyhouse humidity.

classes.name: Target spot
classes.symptoms: Small brown lesions enlarging into ringed spots on leaves, stems and fruit.

classes.name: Yellow leaf curl virus
classes.symptoms: Severe upward cupping, yellow leaf margins, stunted bushy plants, heavy flower drop.

classes.name: Mosaic virus
classes.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling, fern-leaf narrowing and puckering of young leaves.

classes.name: Early blight
classes.symptoms: Concentric ringed brown lesions on older leaves, progressive defoliation from the base upward.

classes.name: Late blight
classes.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked dark lesions with a pale halo, white sporulation on the underside, whole-canopy collapse in cool wet spells.

classes.name: Rice blast
classes.symptoms: Spindle / eye-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown margins; neck blast blackens the panicle base and empties grain.

classes.name: Bacterial leaf blight
classes.symptoms: Yellow wavy-margined streaks from the leaf tip drying downward; milky bacterial ooze from a cut leaf held in water.

classes.name: Brown spot
classes.symptoms: Numerous oval brown spots with grey centres on the blade; strongly associated with nutrient-poor or drought-stressed soils.

classes.name: Sheath blight
classes.symptoms: Oval greenish-grey water-soaked lesions on the sheath near the water line, with irregular purple-brown borders and banded 'snake-skin' patterning.

classes.name: Tungro
classes.symptoms: Orange-yellow discolouration from the leaf tip, stunting, reduced tillering, patchy field distribution.

classes.name: Leaf (brown) rust
classes.symptoms: Round to oval orange-brown powdery pustules scattered mainly on the upper leaf surface.

classes.name: Stripe (yellow) rust
classes.symptoms: Bright yellow pustules in long stripes between the veins; explosive in cool humid north-Indian winters.

classes.name: Powdery mildew
classes.symptoms: White to grey cottony powdery patches on the upper surface of lower leaves, later with black cleistothecia.

classes.name: Septoria leaf blotch
classes.symptoms: Elongated tan blotches confined between veins, speckled with dark pycnidia.

classes.name: Common rust
classes.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown powdery pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces, darkening with age.

classes.name: Northern leaf blight
classes.symptoms: Long grey-green cigar-shaped lesions running parallel to the veins, starting on lower leaves.

classes.name: Grey leaf spot
classes.symptoms: Narrow rectangular tan lesions with straight edges sharply bounded by the leaf veins.

classes.name: Bacterial blight (angular leaf spot)
classes.symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by the veins, turning brown-black; black arm on stems and boll rot.

classes.name: Cotton leaf curl virus
classes.symptoms: Upward or downward leaf curling, thickened darkened veins, cup-shaped enations on the underside, stunting.

classes.name: Alternaria leaf spot
classes.symptoms: Small brown circular spots with concentric rings and a purple margin, coalescing and causing defoliation.

classes.name: Chilli leaf curl complex
classes.agent: Chilli leaf curl virus (whitefly / thrips complex)
classes.symptoms: Severe upward curling and crinkling, shortened internodes, small leathery leaves, 'murda' appearance.

classes.name: Anthracnose / die-back
classes.symptoms: Sunken circular fruit lesions with concentric acervuli rings; twig die-back from the tip downward.

classes.name: Powdery mildew
classes.symptoms: Yellow blotches on the upper surface with white powdery growth on the underside, followed by heavy leaf drop.

classes.name: Red rot
classes.symptoms: Drying of the third/fourth leaf from the top; split cane shows red internal tissue crossed by white transverse patches and an alcoholic sour smell.

classes.name: Rust
classes.symptoms: Elongated orange-brown pustules on the lower leaf surface, leaves drying prematurely.

classes.name: Yellow leaf disease
classes.symptoms: Intense yellowing of the midrib on the underside spreading into the lamina, tip necrosis, reduced growth.

classes.name: Downy mildew
classes.symptoms: Yellow translucent oil spots on the upper surface with white downy sporulation directly beneath after dew or rain.

classes.name: Powdery mildew
classes.symptoms: Ash-grey powdery coating on leaves, shoots and berries; berries crack and scar.

classes.name: Black rot
classes.symptoms: Circular tan leaf lesions ringed with dark pycnidia; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.

classes.name: Esca (black measles)
classes.symptoms: Interveinal 'tiger-stripe' chlorosis and necrosis, sudden apoplexy of whole arms, dark spotting on berries.

classes.name: Isariopsis leaf blight
classes.symptoms: Irregular dark brown angular blotches with a paler centre, heavy defoliation late in the season.

classes.name: Fall armyworm
classes.symptoms: Ragged whorl feeding with windowpane scarring, wet sawdust-like frass in the whorl, inverted Y on the head capsule and four dorsal spots on the last segment.

etl.note: 5-10% whorl damage in early whorl, 10-20% in late whorl (ICAR-NCIPM)

classes.name: American bollworm / gram pod borer
classes.symptoms: Circular bore holes in bolls and pods with the larva's head inserted and body outside; flower and square shedding.

etl.note: 1 larva/plant or 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive nights

classes.name: Pink bollworm
classes.symptoms: Rosetted flowers, interlocked lint, pink larvae inside bolls, exit holes plugged with frass.

etl.note: 8 moths/pheromone trap/night for 3 nights, or 10% rosette flowers

classes.name: Whitefly
classes.symptoms: Clouds of tiny white adults flying up when the canopy is disturbed, nymphs on the underside, sooty mould on honeydew; vector of leaf-curl viruses.

etl.note: 6 adults/leaf on the top 3 leaves (cotton); much lower where leaf curl virus is present

classes.name: Aphid
classes.symptoms: Dense colonies of soft-bodied insects on tender shoots and leaf undersides, curling, sticky honeydew and black sooty mould, ants in attendance.

classes.name: Green leafhopper
classes.symptoms: Green hoppers at the canopy top; feeding scars and, more importantly, transmission of rice tungro.

etl.note: 2 hoppers/hill where tungro is endemic, 10-20 otherwise

classes.name: Brown planthopper
classes.symptoms: Brown hoppers clustered at the base of tillers just above the water line; circular patches of dried plants ('hopper burn') spreading outward.

etl.note: 10 hoppers/hill before flowering, 20/hill after, when spiders are absent

classes.name: Yellow stem borer
classes.symptoms: Dead heart in the vegetative stage (central shoot dries and pulls out easily), white ear head at the panicle stage.

classes.name: Rice leaf folder
classes.symptoms: Leaves folded lengthwise and stitched with silk, white longitudinal scraped streaks where the larva has fed inside.

etl.note: 10% damaged leaves, or 2 freshly damaged leaves/hill

classes.name: Thrips
classes.symptoms: Silvery streaks and black faecal specks, upward leaf curling and crinkling, deformed buds; vector of viral leaf-curl complexes.

classes.name: Two-spotted spider mite
classes.symptoms: Fine white stippling giving a bronzed dusty look, faint webbing on the underside; worst in hot dry weather and after broad-spectrum sprays.

etl.note: 10 mites/leaf, or webbing visible on 10% of leaves

classes.name: Mealybug
classes.symptoms: White waxy cottony masses on stems, leaf axils and undersides; bunchy stunted growth, honeydew and sooty mould, ants tending the colonies.

etl.note: 10% plants infested, or colonies on 5% of terminals

classes.name: Tomato leaf miner (Tuta)
classes.symptoms: Irregular blotch mines in the lamina with black frass inside, pin-hole entries into fruit near the calyx.

classes.name: Early shoot borer
classes.symptoms: Dead hearts in shoots up to four months old that pull out easily and smell offensive; bore holes near ground level.

classes.name: Nitrogen deficiency
classes.symptoms: Uniform pale green to yellow starting on the OLDEST lower leaves and moving up; whole plant stunted and spindly.

classes.name: Phosphorus deficiency
classes.symptoms: Dull blue-green older leaves with purple or reddish tints on the underside and along veins; delayed flowering, thin stems.

classes.name: Potassium deficiency
classes.symptoms: Scorching and browning of the MARGINS of older leaves with the mid-lamina staying green; weak lodging-prone stems.

classes.name: Zinc deficiency
classes.symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis with rusty brown blotches on middle leaves, shortened internodes and small leaves; 'khaira' in rice on calcareous / high-pH soils.

classes.name: Iron deficiency
classes.symptoms: Sharp interveinal chlorosis on the YOUNGEST leaves with veins staying distinctly green; severe cases bleach white.

classes.name: Magnesium deficiency
classes.symptoms: Interveinal yellowing on OLDER leaves in an inverted-V pattern from the margin inward, veins remaining green.

classes.name: Water stress (drought)
classes.symptoms: Leaf rolling or inward folding, dull grey-green canopy, wilting that persists into the morning, marginal drying without lesions.

classes.name: Heat stress / sunscald
classes.symptoms: Bleached papery patches on sun-exposed tissue, necrotic leaf tips and margins, flower and fruit drop after a heat spell.

classes.name: Waterlogging / flood damage
classes.symptoms: Uniform yellowing from the bottom up after standing water, epinastic drooping petioles, silt-coated leaves, root blackening and rot.

classes.name: Healthy soybean
classes.symptoms: Uniform green trifoliate leaves, no mottling or pustules.

classes.name: Healthy mango
classes.symptoms: Dark green leathery leaves, clean panicles, no sooty coating.

classes.name: Healthy citrus
classes.symptoms: Glossy dark green leaves with a symmetric blade, no mottling or corky lesions.

classes.name: Soybean rust
classes.symptoms: Small angular tan lesions on the underside bearing raised volcano-shaped pustules; rapid defoliation from the bottom up.

classes.name: Bacterial blight
classes.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked spots with a yellow halo that dry to brown and tear out, leaving a ragged leaf.

classes.name: Frogeye leaf spot
classes.symptoms: Circular spots with grey centres and a distinct reddish-brown ring, mostly on the upper leaves.

classes.name: Anthracnose
classes.symptoms: Irregular brown blotches on stems and pods studded with black setae-bearing acervuli; pods stay flat and empty.

classes.name: Yellow mosaic
classes.symptoms: Bright yellow irregular patches interspersed with green, spreading until whole leaflets turn golden; pods small and distorted.

classes.name: Anthracnose
classes.symptoms: Black sunken spots on leaves, blossom blight that blackens the panicle, and expanding black rot on ripening fruit.

classes.name: Powdery mildew
classes.symptoms: White powdery coating on panicles, young fruit and leaf undersides, followed by heavy flower and fruitlet drop.

classes.name: Malformation
classes.symptoms: Compact bunched shoots with shortened internodes, or a dense sterile panicle of stunted flowers that sets no fruit.

classes.name: Sooty mould
classes.agent: Capnodium spp. growing on insect honeydew
classes.symptoms: Black soot-like film wiping off the leaf surface; always secondary to hoppers, mealybug or scale feeding above.

classes.name: Bacterial black spot / canker
classes.symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots turning black and raised, often with a yellow halo, and star-shaped cracks on fruit.

classes.name: Citrus greening (HLB)
classes.symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottle that ignores the veins, yellow shoots on one limb, small lopsided fruit with aborted brown seeds.

classes.name: Citrus canker
classes.symptoms: Raised corky brown lesions with an oily margin and a yellow halo, on both leaf surfaces, twigs and fruit.

classes.name: Gummosis / foot rot
classes.symptoms: Amber gum oozing from bark cracks near the base, bark splitting, and a thinning chlorotic canopy above the affected sector.

classes.name: Citrus scab
classes.symptoms: Corky wart-like raised scabs on leaves and rind, often distorting young leaves into a warped shape.

classes.name: Bacterial leaf spot
classes.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots becoming angular, dark and slightly raised, with the leaf yellowing and dropping early.

classes.name: Tobacco caterpillar (Spodoptera litura)
classes.symptoms: Young larvae skeletonise leaves in a gregarious patch leaving a papery window; older larvae feed at night and hide in soil cracks by day.

classes.name: Beet armyworm
classes.symptoms: Pale green larvae with a fine wavy lateral stripe, scraping the leaf surface and boring into buds.

classes.name: Cutworm
classes.symptoms: Seedlings cut clean off at ground level overnight; fat greasy grey larvae curl into a C when dug up near the stump.

etl.note: 5% seedlings cut, or 1 larva per metre of row

classes.name: Red hairy caterpillar
classes.symptoms: Dense reddish-brown hairy larvae marching in swarms and stripping leaves to the midrib, typically after the first monsoon showers.

classes.name: Hornworm
classes.symptoms: Very large green larva with diagonal side stripes and a horn at the tail; heavy defoliation of the top of the plant plus large dark frass pellets.

classes.name: Pod borer
classes.symptoms: Neat round exit holes in pods with frass at the entry; opened pods show a larva and partly eaten seed.

classes.name: Stem borer
classes.symptoms: Central shoot dries into a dead heart that pulls out easily; the split stem shows a tunnel packed with frass.

classes.name: Shoot and fruit borer
classes.symptoms: Wilted drooping shoot tips with a bore hole and frass; fruit shows a plugged entry hole and internal tunnelling.

classes.name: Pyralid borer
classes.symptoms: Webbed and tied leaves or bored stems with frass at the entry, the larva concealed inside the shelter.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Looper / semilooper
classes.symptoms: Caterpillars that arch the body into a loop as they walk, chewing ragged holes between the veins.

classes.name: Leafroller / leaf tier
classes.symptoms: Leaves rolled or tied with silk into a tube, the larva feeding inside on the enclosed surface.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Bagworm
classes.symptoms: Spindle-shaped cases of silk and leaf fragments hanging from twigs, moving as the larva inside feeds.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Citrus butterfly (lemon butterfly)
classes.symptoms: Young larvae mimic bird droppings, older ones are large and green with eyespots; they strip flush leaves on young citrus.

etl.note: 2 larvae/plant on nursery and young trees

classes.name: Leafhopper / jassid
classes.agent: Cicadellidae - Amrasca biguttula biguttula (cotton jassid), Empoasca spp.
classes.symptoms: Wedge-shaped green hoppers that run sideways; leaf margins yellow then turn red-brown and cup downward ('hopper burn').

classes.name: Planthopper
classes.symptoms: Hoppers clustered low on the stem, sooty mould on their honeydew, and circular drying patches spreading through the field.

classes.name: Citrus psyllid
classes.symptoms: Tiny brown adults resting at 45 degrees on flush, yellow nymphs excreting white waxy tubules; the vector of citrus greening.

etl.note: Any psyllid on flush is actionable where greening is present

classes.name: Mirid bug
classes.symptoms: Slender green bugs feeding on squares and terminals; damaged squares shed and terminals become blind and bushy.

classes.name: Stink bug
classes.symptoms: Shield-shaped bugs on pods and grain; feeding punctures leave sunken corky spots and shrivelled or discoloured seed.

etl.note: 1 bug/m row on soybean at pod fill

classes.name: Lanternfly
classes.symptoms: Large planthoppers massing on trunks and canes with copious honeydew and sooty mould beneath.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Scale insect
classes.symptoms: Immobile waxy or armoured bumps on twigs, leaves and fruit that scrape off to reveal the insect; honeydew and sooty mould below.

classes.name: Eriophyid mite
classes.symptoms: Microscopic mites causing erineum felt patches, bud proliferation or silvery russeting; damage is visible long before the mite is.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: White grub
classes.symptoms: Plants wilt and pull out with the roots eaten away; fat C-shaped white grubs with a brown head lie in the root zone.

etl.note: 1 grub/m2, or 10% plants wilting in patches

classes.name: Wireworm
classes.symptoms: Hard shiny orange-brown larvae boring into seed and underground stems, causing patchy stands and wilted seedlings.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Leaf beetle
classes.symptoms: Small hard-shelled beetles chewing round holes or shot-holes and grazing long window-like strips from the leaf.

classes.name: Hadda beetle (epilachna)
classes.symptoms: Adults and spiny yellow grubs both graze the leaf in parallel arcs, leaving a lace-like skeleton of veins.

classes.name: Weevil
classes.symptoms: Snouted beetles notching leaf margins or boring into stems and fruit; larvae tunnel inside unseen.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Longhorn stem borer
classes.symptoms: Long-antennae beetles; larvae tunnel in trunks and main stems, pushing out coarse frass from a round hole and killing the limb above.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Jewel beetle / stem borer
classes.symptoms: Metallic beetles whose flat-headed larvae mine under the bark, leaving a sunken dead strip and dieback of the shoot.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Bark beetle / shot-hole borer
classes.symptoms: Pin-sized round holes in the bark with fine sawdust, and galleries just beneath; attacks trees already under stress.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Grasshopper / locust
classes.symptoms: Ragged chewing from the leaf margin inward, and in outbreaks whole plants stripped to stems within a day.

etl.note: 5 hoppers/m2; any swarm is an emergency

classes.name: Mole cricket
classes.symptoms: Seedlings toppling in rows with severed roots and raised soil tunnels visible after irrigation.
classes.etl_note: Family/genus-level class - no single published economic threshold. Scout, identify the species, and use the threshold your KVK publishes for it.

classes.name: Termite
classes.symptoms: Plants dry and pull out with the roots and stem base eaten hollow and packed with soil; earthen runways up the stem.

classes.name: Snail / slug
classes.symptoms: Irregular holes chewed from the leaf interior with silvery slime trails; damage appears overnight and in damp weather.

etl.note: 2/m2, or fresh slime and holes on 10% of plants
